## {.title-slide}

### Dyna

**Distributed Version Control for Resource Catalogs**

A Pijul-inspired system for collaborative JSON resource editing with S3 storage, changeset-based versioning, and an elfo-rs actor server.

::: {.fragment}
*From monolithic pain to distributed gain.*
:::

---

## SDMF: A Massive Catalog of 40,000+ Resources

The **Semantic Data Modeling Framework** became the backbone of enterprise data architecture — a living catalog of interconnected JSON resources.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

### Scale

- **40,000+** JSON resources
- **Hundreds** of namespaces
- Entities, connectors, threat models
- Semantic mappings and schemas

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

### Resource Types

| Type | Count |
|------|-------|
| Entity Definitions | ~12,000 |
| Connector Configs | ~8,000 |
| Threat Models | ~5,000 |
| Semantic Mappings | ~15,000 |

:::

::::

---

## Users Reported Critical Friction {background-color="#2d2a26"}

::: {style="color: #faf6f0;"}

### The pain was real and growing

1. [**Minutes-long startup**]{.accent} — loading 40K resources into memory at launch
2. [**Destructive overwrites**]{.accent} — no version history, last-write-wins
3. [**No concurrent editing**]{.accent} — single-user lock on the entire catalog
4. [**No branching**]{.accent} — experimental changes polluted production
5. [**Excessive memory pressure**]{.accent} — entire catalog resident in RAM

> "We lost three days of work because someone overwrote the connector namespace. There was no way to recover."

:::

---

## The Vision: Git-Like Version Control for JSON

We envisioned a system where every change is tracked, every branch is isolated, and every client stays in sync.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

### Core Principles

- **Immutable changesets** — content-addressed, tamper-proof
- **Channels** — isolated branches for safe experimentation
- **Distributed sync** — push/pull like Git, but for JSON
- **Lazy loading** — on-demand, not all-at-once

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

### Inspired By

| System | Borrowed Concept |
|--------|-----------------|
| **Pijul** | Patch commutativity |
| **Git** | Content-addressable storage |
| **CouchDB** | JSON-native documents |
| **Nix** | Reproducible builds |

:::

::::

---

## Data Model: Resources → Patches → Changesets → Channels

Four layers, each building on the last — from raw JSON documents to named branches.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 11
graph LR
    R["Resource<br/><i>JSON document</i>"] --> P["Patch<br/><i>RFC 6902 diff + snapshot</i>"]
    P --> CS["Changeset<br/><i>Content-addressed commit</i>"]
    CS --> CH["Channel<br/><i>Named branch with HEAD</i>"]
    style R fill:#c25e30,color:#fff,stroke:#a04820
    style P fill:#2a7a72,color:#fff,stroke:#1d5c56
    style CS fill:#2d2a26,color:#faf6f0,stroke:#1a1816
    style CH fill:#7a7570,color:#fff,stroke:#5a5550
```

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

| Layer | Identity | Immutable? |
|-------|----------|-----------|
| Resource | UUID | No (evolves) |
| Patch | SHA-256 | Yes |
| Changeset | SHA-256 | Yes |
| Channel | Name string | No (HEAD moves) |

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

### RFC 6902 Operations

```json
[
  {"op": "replace", "path": "/role", "value": "admin"},
  {"op": "add", "path": "/permissions/-", "value": "write"},
  {"op": "remove", "path": "/deprecated"}
]
```

:::

::::

## Actor-Based Server with S3 Persistence

The server uses the **elfo** actor framework for fault isolation, clean message-passing, and structured concurrency.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="55%"}

### Actor Hierarchy

| Actor | Responsibility |
|-------|---------------|
| **API Gateway** | HTTP ↔ elfo bridge (axum) |
| **Changeset Manager** | Validation, channels, merge |
| **Storage Actor** | S3 I/O via `object_store` |
| **Notification Actor** | WebSocket broadcast |

### Message Flow

```
HTTP → API Gateway → Changeset Manager → Storage Actor → S3
                                       ↘ Notification Actor → WebSocket
```

:::

::: {.column width="45%"}

### REST Endpoints

| Method | Path |
|--------|------|
| `POST` | `/resources` |
| `GET` | `/resources/:id` |
| `PUT` | `/resources/:id` |
| `DELETE` | `/resources/:id` |
| `POST` | `/changesets` |
| `POST` | `/push` |
| `POST` | `/pull` |
| `POST` | `/clone` |
| `GET` | `/channels` |
| `POST` | `/channels` |
| `WS` | `/ws` |

:::

::::

## Lazy Loading: Minutes → Milliseconds

Instead of loading 40,000 resources at startup, lazy clients fetch only metadata, materialise on-demand, cache locally, and receive real-time updates.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

### Traditional Loading

```
Startup: Load ALL 40K resources
         ├── Fetch from S3        ~45s
         ├── Deserialize JSON     ~30s
         ├── Build index          ~15s
         └── Ready                ~90s total
         Memory: ~2.4 GB resident
```

### Lazy Loading

```
Startup: Connect + fetch metadata
         ├── WebSocket connect    ~50ms
         ├── List resource IDs    ~200ms
         └── Ready                ~250ms total
         Memory: ~12 MB baseline
```

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

### On-Demand Materialisation

1. User requests resource by ID
2. Client fetches patches from server
3. Replays RFC 6902 operations
4. Caches materialised snapshot
5. Subsequent reads hit local cache

### Cache Invalidation

- WebSocket push on changeset commit
- Client re-materialises affected resources
- Delivers `UpdateEvent` with full metadata

:::

::::

---

## Lazy Loaders in Four Languages

Identical semantics across Rust, Go, Python, and WebAssembly — connect, list, get, subscribe.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

### Rust (lazy-cat)

```rust
let client = LazyClient::connect(url).await?;
let ids = client.list_resources().await?;
let resource = client.get_resource(&id).await?;
client.on_update(|event| {
    println!("Updated: {:?}", event.affected_resources);
}).await;
```

### Go (lazy-go)

```go
client := lazydyna.NewClient(url)
client.Connect(ctx)
ids, _ := client.ListResources(ctx)
res, _ := client.GetResource(ctx, id)
client.OnUpdate(func(e UpdateEvent) {
    fmt.Printf("Updated: %v\n", e.AffectedResources)
})
```

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

### Python (lazy-py)

```python
async with LazyClient(url) as client:
    ids = await client.list_resources()
    resource = await client.get_resource(id)
    async for event in client.updates():
        print(f"Updated: {event.affected_resources}")
```

### WASM (lazy-wasm)

```javascript
const client = await LazyWasmClient.new(url);
const ids = client.list_resources();
const resource = client.get_resource(id);
client.on_update((event) => {
    console.log("Updated:", event.affected_resources);
});
```

:::

::::

## Real-Time Collaboration via WebSocket

Changes propagate to all connected clients within milliseconds. Every client receives rich `UpdateEvent` objects with full changeset metadata.

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 11
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Client A (Rust CLI)
    participant S as Dyna Server
    participant B as Client B (Go)
    participant C as Client C (Elm UI)

    A->>S: POST /push (changeset)
    S->>S: Validate & store in S3
    S-->>A: 200 OK
    par WebSocket broadcast
        S-->>B: UpdateEvent { changeset, affected_resources }
        S-->>C: UpdateEvent { changeset, affected_resources }
    end
    B->>B: Re-materialise affected resources
    C->>C: Re-materialise & update UI
```

### UpdateEvent Structure

```json
{
  "changeset_id": "sha256:a1b2c3...",
  "author": "alice",
  "channel": "main",
  "affected_resources": ["res-001", "res-042"],
  "operations_count": 5,
  "timestamp": "2026-03-05T10:30:00Z"
}
```

## Browser UI: Elm + WebAssembly

Two browser applications for visual resource management — **dyna-app** for full CRUD editing and **lazy-elm-demo** for lazy-loading demonstration.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

### dyna-app (Full Editor)

- Elm 0.19 + WASM bridge via ports
- Create, read, update, delete resources
- Channel management (create, switch, promote)
- Changeset history and diff viewer
- Real-time sync via WebSocket

### Architecture

```
Elm App ←→ Ports ←→ JS Bridge ←→ WASM Client
                                      ↕
                                 Dyna Server
```

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

### lazy-elm-demo (Lazy Viewer)

- Two-panel layout with scrollable resource list
- JSON detail view with syntax highlighting
- Live update log with changeset metadata
- On-demand resource materialisation
- Minimal memory footprint

### Key Features

| Feature | Implementation |
|---------|---------------|
| Resource list | Scrollable, click-to-select |
| Detail view | Pretty-printed JSON |
| Live updates | Streaming event log |
| Lazy fetch | WASM `get_resource()` |

:::

::::

## Reproducible Builds: One Nix Flake, 24+ Packages

The entire ecosystem — server, CLI, clients, demos, OCI images — is built and deployed from a single `flake.nix`.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

### Package Matrix

| Package | Language | Builder |
|---------|----------|---------|
| dyna-core | Rust | crane |
| dyna-server | Rust | crane |
| dyna-cli | Rust | crane |
| dyna-wasm | Rust→WASM | wasm-pack |
| dyna-py | Rust→Python | maturin |
| dyna-go | Go | buildGoModule |
| dyna-app | Elm | elmPackages |
| lazy-cat | Rust | crane |
| lazy-go | Go | buildGoModule |
| lazy-py | Rust→Python | maturin |
| lazy-wasm | Rust→WASM | wasm-pack |
| lazy-elm-demo | Elm | elmPackages |

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

### Build Commands

```bash
# Build everything
nix build .#all

# Build specific package
nix build .#dyna-server

# Run demo
nix run .#lazy-cat-demo

# Development shell
nix develop

# OCI image
nix build .#dyna-server-oci
docker load < result
```

### Guarantees

- **Hermetic** — no ambient system dependencies
- **Reproducible** — same inputs → same outputs
- **Cacheable** — Nix binary cache for CI
- **Cross-platform** — Linux, macOS, WASM

:::

## Roadmap: What Comes Next

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

### Near Term

- **Three-way merge** — automatic conflict resolution for non-overlapping edits
- **Partial namespace sync** — subscribe to subsets of the catalog
- **JSON Schema validation** — enforce resource structure at commit time
- **Incremental materialisation** — apply only new patches, skip replayed history

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

### Long Term

- **Federated catalogs** — multi-server sync across organizational boundaries
- **Conflict resolution UI** — visual merge tool in the Elm app
- **Performance benchmarks** — published comparisons of full vs. lazy loading
- **Branch/merge operations** — Git-like workflows with channel promotion

:::

::::

::: {.fragment}

### Design Principles Going Forward

> Every feature must preserve the core invariants: immutable changesets, content-addressable storage, and lazy-by-default loading.

:::
